title: fix(plugins): keep official installs trusted when Doctor runs from home
body:
Fixes #178589
Supersedes #178643, thanks @pattty847.

## What Problem This Solves

Doctor run from the home directory can report an official installed Codex plugin as unverified and recommend an unnecessary reinstall or repair.

## User Impact

Installed plugins keep their global provenance when the workspace's extensions directory resolves to the same directory. Doctor can inspect the official installation regardless of whether it runs from home or the state directory. No configuration change or migration is required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The workspace scan ran before the global scan and claimed the same physical plugin entry. Discovery now leaves the overlapping root to its existing global/install-record owner, using the existing physical-directory comparison. Explicit load paths, ordinary workspace discovery, and official-install verification keep their existing behavior.

Production: +6/-9 (net -3); tests: +40/-0; docs: +1/-0. The existing identical UID return guards were combined, and the regression lives in the smaller discovery-provenance sibling suite. No baseline or suppression changed; the line-cap ratchet passes.

## Evidence

- The home-workspace regression in `discovery-checkout.test.ts` fails on the unchanged base with `origin: "workspace"` and missing `trustedOfficialInstall`; the state-directory control passes. The final two discovery suites pass all 69 tests (42.75 s wall in Vitest, 4% test time; 35.30 s shared compiler preparation).
- Isolated source Doctor command-handler proof, with synthetic plugin files and official install metadata persisted through the normal installed-index owner: home and state-directory runs both return `{"schemaVersion":1,"ok":true,"checksRun":1,"checksSkipped":2,"findings":[]}`. The unchanged discovery code's real Doctor resolver rejects the same home-directory installation as unverified. No operator state or running Gateway was modified.
- Commands: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/discovery.test.ts src/plugins/discovery-checkout.test.ts --maxWorkers=1`; source Doctor harness invokes `runDoctorLintCli` with `onlyIds: ["codex/provenance-probe"]` from each directory under an isolated HOME and OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR.
- Targeted core and plugin-test typechecks, type-aware lint, formatting, `git diff --check`, and the import-cycle check pass (0 cycles). Independent Codex review found no actionable P0–P2 issues. The required direct-import consumer sweep and two Doctor sibling suites passed 684 tests across 41 files in 453.68 s (7 shards); the initial discovery run brought that to 735 tests across 42 unique files. The final focused rerun above covers the relocated regression and equivalent UID-guard cleanup. The inherited runtime-config shard passed 140 tests in 178.32 s; `io.write-config.test.ts` accounted for 103 cases and 111.369 s summed test time (longest case 10.894 s). It exercises durable writes with per-case state cleanup. No test timeout was increased.

The full `pnpm openclaw doctor` wrapper refused artifact publication because it could not verify an offline Gateway on this host; its guard was preserved. This proof uses the real source command handler and synthetic installed plugin, not a packaged upgrade or authenticated Codex session. The full `check:changed` SQLite inventory was omitted under the local gate budget; targeted type, lint, format, tests, and import-cycle checks are used instead, with PR CI providing broad coverage.
